# v0.3.0 launch acceptance

Published and verified on 2026-10-11. This record distinguishes candidate testing from the completed public-tag and deployment checks. Public announcement remains the maintainer's decision.

## Foundation

The engineering baseline is `110faa4f7add774922eb6bfd0cf1f47e32660cb9`.

| Change | Merged PR |
| --- | --- |
| Preserve complete team and seed files, deletions, dependencies and generated adapter receipts during updates | [#50](https://github.com/itspatmorgan/design-studio-starter/pull/50) |
| Enforce module boundaries and remove the shared shell's private Manual import | [#51](https://github.com/itspatmorgan/design-studio-starter/pull/51) |
| Build with each optional module enabled, disabled and physically removed | [#52](https://github.com/itspatmorgan/design-studio-starter/pull/52) |
| Cut over all public API consumers and make the module entry safe in Node | [#53](https://github.com/itspatmorgan/design-studio-starter/pull/53) |
| Compare semantic contracts and runtime requirements against supported releases | [#54](https://github.com/itspatmorgan/design-studio-starter/pull/54) |
| Exercise the actual update CLI and require upgrade success for upstream PRs | [#55](https://github.com/itspatmorgan/design-studio-starter/pull/55) |
| Remove obsolete conversion commands, readers, helpers, dependency and empty directories | [#56](https://github.com/itspatmorgan/design-studio-starter/pull/56) |

The baseline passed 488 release tests, the actual CLI update rehearsal, frozen installation, synchronization, formatting, module checks, released-contract checks, strict ownership, production build and asset inspection. [Required CI passed](https://github.com/itspatmorgan/design-studio-starter/actions/runs/38187471096). The removal matrix covers all six optional modules individually disabled and removed. Upgrade acceptance covers dry-run invariants, exact merge/stamp, protected content and deletion, dependency and adapter preservation, conflict/continue, and honest failed-check reporting. Synthetic post-launch tests enforce the chosen compatibility policy; historical pre-release tags are not supported baselines.

## Live installation journeys

The isolated installation source is `1894dbe5066482066e0771549c84564fff1d5a15`: the engineering baseline plus proposed installation and publishing guidance. Its local `v0.3.0` tag is a private test candidate. It does not prove availability of the eventual public tag.

Tests use macOS with Git 2.54.0, mise, Node 24.14.1 and pnpm 12.8.2 already installed, warm caches and existing harness accounts. Each journey follows the repository guide without a plugin installer, preserves an occupied destination marker, clones full ancestry into an alternate folder, registers a fictional contributor without a GitHub account, retains samples, selects Product explicitly and creates a counter prototype. Parent browser QA verifies the rendered heading and button interaction. The harnesses leave authoring changes uncommitted for review.

| Harness | Installation and authoring | Fresh-session reopening |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex CLI 0.151.0 | Passed, including browser interaction and checks | Passed; configuration, contributor, permanent IDs and uncommitted files preserved |
| Claude Code 2.1.152 | Passed after local sign-in, including browser interaction and checks | Passed; configuration, contributor, permanent IDs, uncommitted work and preview preserved |
| Cursor 3.24.12 | Passed in the local fixture, including browser interaction and checks | Passed in a new chat after selecting the installed folder; all 848 source entries preserved |

Codex's configured default model was unavailable to this account. The acceptance invocation used `gpt-5.6-sol`; global settings were preserved. Claude Code initially reported that it was not logged in; the user completed login before the retry. Cursor retains the user's selected Grok 4.7 High model. Its native Open Workspace flow selected the installed folder before a new chat. The first clone encountered sandbox hook creation restrictions; the agent inspected the partial destination and retried the scoped command with permission. A proposed check wrapper used zsh's readonly `status` variable; the runner skipped it and supplied a correction. The subsequent check commands passed. Sandbox requests are approved for individual scoped fixture commands, without broadening global permissions. Noninteractive harness background previews were handed to the parent acceptance runner for the reopening checks. An initial Claude reopening found the terminated preview and correctly reported failure; after the runner restarted it, a new session passed. Use `pnpm dev --host ... --port ...` for additional Vite flags; inserting another `--` prevents those flags from reaching Vite correctly. Contributor profiles use an empty GitHub string when no account is supplied, as required by the current validator.

## Team collaboration

An isolated clone registered a fictional owner, switched to Team mode with that owner's permanent Admin ID, then registered an ordinary contributor. The contributor created and authored their own explicitly Product-assigned prototype. The context CLI resolved its owner, source folder, system instructions and permanent IDs for code handoff. Checks and production build passed; the local counter rendered and incremented in light and dark modes without browser errors.

The contributor's attempted shared configuration change failed before writing. A request to the real local system-source editing service returned HTTP 403 for an unassigned system write. The system source bytes and settings remained unchanged. These are local workflow boundaries, not authentication or Git-provider access controls.

## Publishing

The Sites publishing acceptance fixture contains fictional learning examples in an isolated full clone. It validates the optional publishing workflow; the ongoing public demo remains the [custom-domain GitHub Pages deployment](https://itspatmorgan.com/design-studio-starter/). It uses native Sites static publishing, with `dist/` and SPA fallback, and preserves the project identity in its local `.openai/hosting.json`. No hosted editing backend, Worker or MCP service is required.

Native deployment succeeded for the first publication and two updates to the same project and URL. Version 3 uses source `3eb9005c69fc780d6d602ca27c995e6dfcb7dac9`, packaged from that pushed commit. Its 519-file archive has SHA-256 `9d780ffb85e5a17ce990ede690c0d2508f793202e6c694963e99a9e330bfd21e`. The project remained public. A visitor session stayed open during the final update, continued navigating the old loaded application, then reloaded and displayed the new tagline. Anonymous HTTP retrieval and browser checks passed for Home, a prototype interaction, document, Manual, Product system, Mermaid diagram and canvas, including direct reloads. Browser error logs were empty.

Sites' SPA fallback returns HTML with HTTP 200 for missing asset URLs. Referenced build assets exist and loaded successfully; strict missing-asset 404 behavior is not claimed for Sites. Team hosts should configure application rewrites without replacing asset 404 responses. Existing large-chunk warnings remain; baseline entry JavaScript/CSS is 716.0 KiB raw and 87.7 KiB gzip across two files. This diagnostic excludes lazy features and is not a network timing measurement.

The installed 0.2.0-beta.1 Design Studio plugin's publishing wrapper expects the old layout. This launch validates repository installation and native Sites publishing; it does not claim that obsolete wrapper works with the new foundation. Plugin release, provider-specific Vercel/Cloudflare/Netlify walkthroughs, clean-computer installation and the separately arranged existing-studio pilot are deferred.
